fixes.explanation: Paul, who calls himself an apostle at the start of this letter (Romans 1:1), says, “I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.” He didn't just say he was an Israelite. He brought the whole family tree with him. If anybody has a right to talk about Israel, it's the man with the paperwork.

Close, friend, but Paul doesn't say Judah. He says he's “…from the tribe of Benjamin.” Judah was one of Israel's twelve tribes too (Genesis 49:8, 28), but the text doesn't put Paul in it. It's an easy swap, like grabbing the wrong cookie tin off the shelf.

Paul doesn't name Levi here. He says, “I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.” So Benjamin is the tribe on his family tree. Levi was another of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 49:5, 28), but Paul isn't pointing to it.

That's what Elijah, a prophet of Israel, says to God: “I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well…” He has just said that the prophets are killed and the altars are torn down. Then he says he's the only one left. I think that's a lonely thing to say, friend. He's telling it to God, though, and that matters.

God's reply was, “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.” Baal was a false god (1 Kings 18:21, 39). Elijah said he was the only one left, and God points to seven thousand. Elijah was off on his count, and God did the reserving.

That's a fun story, but it isn't in this reply. God says He reserved these men for Himself, and what marks them is that they “…have not bowed the knee to Baal.” Baal was a false god (1 Kings 18:21, 39). The verse doesn't say a word about hiding prophets.

Nice thought, friend, but the reply doesn't say that. God says, “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.” Baal was a false god (1 Kings 18:21, 39). What stands out about these men is who they did not bow to.

That's the phrase, word for word: “…eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.” Seeing and hearing are exactly what's missing, friend. Paul says it's “…as it is written…” so he's pointing back to Scripture.
